audit.whatIsWrong: win[] and phases[].side gave Gwen levels 1 and 4-5 and marked level 6 as even, contradicting whys[0], whys[3] and whys[4].
audit.why: At level 1 neither has a combo; at 4-5 Rupture's range and knockup let him shove and zone a short-range melee; at 6 Feast is flat true damage that Hallowed Mist's resistances do nothing about. The prose already said all three.
audit.corrected: Skill / Gwen / Gwen / Skill / Cho'Gath / Gwen / Gwen.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns on a page whose central instructions are 'bait the silence' and 'only all-in when his R is down'.
audit.why: Feral Scream is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9, Rupture 6s flat, Vorpal Spikes 8/7/6/5/4 and Feast 80/70/60 against your 13s Skip 'n Slash. A 9-11 second silence and an 80-second Feast are very different waits, and the page treated both as 'when it is down'.
audit.corrected: early, mid, whys[4] and spikes[1].text now carry the numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vorpal Spikes is absent from the entire page, and Feral Scream's silence is only mentioned as 'locking me down' without saying what it actually costs you.
audit.why: Vorpal Spikes adds a slowing ranged spike to his autos, so he chips and slows you from inside his own wave with no commitment - that is why the 'dash in, snip, dash out' pattern is not free. Feral Scream's silence specifically denies Skip 'n Slash and Hallowed Mist, which are your entry and your only escape, so eating it mid-dash is what turns a trade into a death.
audit.corrected: early and wants.foe[1] now name Vorpal Spikes; mid states that the silence takes both your dash and your mist.

edits.before: Cho'Gath is one of my favorite picks to bully — his giant HP bar is exactly what Snip Snip! eats, since the cone deals %-max-HP magic and the center snip is true damage, both ignoring the armor he stacks. Level 1 is a wash, so I just farm and sidestep his Rupture (Q); that delayed knockup is his only real punish, and if I dodge it he can't follow up. From level 2-3 I poke with Q and reset Skip 'n Slash off the hit to dash back out, and his answer is Feral Scream (W) — I bait that cone silence before I commit so it doesn't lock me down mid-trade.
edits.after: Cho'Gath is a bully target — his giant HP bar is exactly what Snip Snip! eats, since the cone deals %-max-HP magic and the centre snip is true damage, both ignoring the armour he stacks. Level 1 is a wash, so farm and sidestep Rupture (Q, 6s); that delayed knockup is his only real punish. From 2-3 poke with Q and refund Skip 'n Slash off the hit to dash back out, but respect Vorpal Spikes chipping and slowing you from inside his own wave, and bait Feral Scream (W, 11s) before you commit — that silence takes both your dash and your mist.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are even because he can shove with Rupture and zone me off CS with his longer range while I'm still a short-range melee, so I respect his Q and farm for my item spike. The big trap is level 6: his Feast (R) is a flat true-damage nuke that executes me outright below the threshold, so even though I out-trade him all lane, fighting him under half HP gets me deleted — and Hallowed Mist's armor/MR does nothing against true damage. I keep snipping his health from range, drop Mist for the untargetability against his autos, and only all-in when his R is down or I'm healthy.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are even because he can shove with Rupture and zone you off CS with his longer range while you are still a short-range melee, so respect his Q and farm for your item spike. The big trap is level 6: Feast (R, 80s at rank 1) is flat true damage that kills you outright if it exceeds your current HP, so even though you out-trade him all lane, fighting him under half gets you deleted — and Hallowed Mist's armour and MR do nothing against true damage. Keep snipping his health, drop Mist for untargetability against his autos, and only all-in when his R is down or you are healthy.

edits.before: This is my house — the fatter he stacks Feast the harder my Thousand Cuts autos and %-HP Snip hit, and my passive heals more the bigger his HP bar gets, so his scaling literally feeds me. Hallowed Mist gives me armor/MR and dodges his single-target auto follow-up while I grind him down, and his stacked armor is worthless against my magic-and-true package. The one rule never changes: a fully-stacked Cho still has a flat true-damage Feast execute that ignores my sustain, so I never duel him at low HP — I open every fight with him healthy, snip him to nothing, and finish before his R flips an extended trade.
edits.after: This is your house — the fatter he stacks Feast the harder your A Thousand Cuts autos and %-HP Snip hit, and your passive heals more the bigger his HP bar gets, so his scaling literally feeds you. Hallowed Mist gives armour and MR and dodges his single-target auto follow-up while you grind him down, and his stacked armour is worthless against your magic-and-true package. One rule never changes: a fully stacked Cho's Feast is flat true damage that ignores your sustain, so never duel him low — open every fight healthy, snip him to nothing, and finish inside his 80s R window.

notes: The content block is written in first person ('one of my favorite picks to bully', 'he can't follow up'); converted early, mid, late and the whys to second person. Level chart corrected at three stages to match the prose: whys[0] says level 1 is even, whys[3] says 4-5 even out, whys[4] says 6 is clearly his - all three were marked Gwen. I did NOT take the packet's suggested 'Skill' at First item, because whys[5] and spikes[2] both say the Riftmaker/Nashor's spike is Gwen's peak and I have no reason to overrule them. Vorpal Spikes (E) is never mentioned anywhere on the page even though it is the ability that lets a melee-range Cho'Gath chip and slow you from behind his own minions - added. Feast is described as an execute 'below the threshold'; it is flat true damage that kills you if it exceeds your current HP, which is a meaningfully different thing to plan around, so the wording is tightened. 'Thousand Cuts' was missing its 'A'.
